title: The winds from HL Tau
question: What are the properties (morphology, opening angle, velocity, energetics) of the outflowing molecular gas from HL Tau, in context with the optical jet and the disk?

data.angular_resolution: CO tapered beam 0.98 x 0.90 arcsec, PA -9 deg
data.sensitivity: CO rms 8.1 mJy/beam per 1 km/s channel; continuum 0.01 mJy/beam

what.value: Disk inclination 46±0.2 deg from continuum uv fitting

evidence.quote: (cite: Brogan15) fit the $uv$ plane visibilities of the dust continuum emission, and found an inclination angle of $46\pm0.2^\circ$

recipe.method: Zeroth and first moment maps clipped at 3 and 5 sigma, integrated over 0-5.5 (blue) and 7-20 km/s (red)
Limb-brightened red lobe decomposed into 90 deg small-scale and 60 deg larger-scale opening angles
Per-channel LTE column density and mass, momentum, energy summed; luminosity and mass loss rate from dynamical age
key_parameters: Velocity integration limits 9-20 km/s red, -4 to 6 km/s blue
assumptions: Optically thin CO, T=50 K, CO abundance 1e-4, distance 140 pc

recipe.method: Solve two trigonometric equations using red and blue peak velocities of counter-flow components with inclination and opening angle
assumptions: Flow axis perpendicular to disk; inclination 44 deg to line of sight

answer_key.quantity: Red lobe opening angle, small scale

evidence.quote: one with a small scale opening angle of 90$^\circ$

answer_key.quantity: Red lobe opening angle, large scale

evidence.quote: a larger scale (collimated) opening angle of of 60$^\circ$
we find red and blue shifted wind velocities of 2.5 and -2.3 km s$^{-1}$.
we derive an outflow age of approximately 2650 yrs.

not_stated_but_needed: Taper parameters used for the released CO cube
Beam counts/areas and exact method for flux to K conversion
Wind and counter-flow peak velocities read from spectra
score_reason: Public data with released images and clear formulae, but several parameters unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple recipe, numeric results.
